title: Consolidation Without Weights: What the Complementary Learning Systems Analogy Licenses in LLM Agent Memory, and Why the Systems That Borrow Its Name Do Not Inherit Its Guarantee
mechanism: Add a weight-free 'replay-then-reindex' consolidation pass: periodically resample high-salience episodic traces (via existing outcome-ledger Wilson-lower-bound credit) and re-run them through the existing MDL consolidation gate in enforcing mode (not shadow), writing derived semantic triplets rather than modifying embeddings/weights — mirrors the paper's CLS claim that consolidation is a replay-driven reindexing process, not weight change, which is exactly the gap chitta has (MDL gate exists but fail-open/shadow-only).

expected_gain.metric: chitta-mcp/server.py recall nDCG@20 on golden set
expected_gain.rationale: chitta already has prefilter (0.435→0.487 nDCG@20 A/B) and MDL gate scaffolding but the gate never enforces (shadow-mode, fail-open per hooks/distill.sh:329-433), so no consolidation-quality signal currently reaches recall; enforcing replay-gated consolidation is a plausible small additional lift, not validated.

evidence.claim: Paper argues CLS-style consolidation in LLM agents is licensed only as replay/reindexing over stored traces, not as a weight-consolidation guarantee (abstract unavailable, title/claim only — not independently verified from full text).
